description: The final format of a Godot game: its released repo and its dataset. Prose: docs/game-format.md. Validator: tools/validate-game.py (repo + dataset contents) with tools/validate-dataset.ps1 (dataset layout). Severity: error = not in the format; warning = a quality rule or something to look at.

repo.what: the game's git repo at its release commit (tracked files only)

required_files.what: the project: its name, main scene, renderer, window size, autoloads and input map; config/features names Godot 4.7
the export presets: "Windows Desktop", and "Android" in a mobile game
the game's scenes; everything the game is made of is committed (scenes/, game/, assets/, addons/), store packs included, every imported file with its .import and every script with its .uid
every generator script that ran, kept unchanged
the game's engine runs through the heavy-job limiter, from the template
the creation record; every row matches docs/schemas/workflow-row.schema.json (godot-workflow/v0)
hero image + captioned gallery of real gameplay stills
every external asset; matches docs/schemas/assets-manifest.schema.json, every listed file committed
Git LFS for every binary type, Godot's text files as text
the engine's cache, build output and the local dataset zip

never_tracked.what: the engine's cache (.godot/) is rebuilt by the first import and never committed
build output, logs and the Gradle build template the Android export installs are never committed
compiled translations are made again at import
a signing keystore is a secret

repo.lfs_why: every binary type of templates/godot-game/.gitattributes goes through Git LFS; Godot's own text files (scenes and resources saved as text, GDScript, shaders, .import and .uid sidecars, project.godot, export_presets.cfg) stay plain git text so they diff and merge: one of them in LFS is an error. Binary content under any other name in plain git is a warning.

sidecars.what: every tracked file Godot 4.7 imports (imported_extensions) has its <file>.import tracked, every tracked file it gives a uid file (uid_extensions: scripts, shaders, and the formats it loads without importing) has its <file>.uid tracked, and every tracked .import or .uid has its file; what the engine skips needs none (a name that starts with a dot, and everything under a folder that holds a .gdignore: Docs/, Dataset/, Brief/, Scripts/)
sidecars.why: the sidecar holds the uid that scenes and resources refer to the file by, and an imported file's import settings: without it the engine writes a new one on the next import and every reference by uid breaks; a sidecar without its file is an orphan

banned_names.what: never inside a game: tool, vendor and owner names (text files of the repo; LFS and binary files are scanned by the packager)

account_name.what: the account (user) name of the machine running the validator, as a word (USERNAME at run time; machine paths carry it): never written in the repo
account_name.why: enforced in workflow.jsonl and every other non-script file; scripts and steps that already ran (Scripts/, steps/, and .ps1/.psm1/.py/.sh/.bat/.cmd files anywhere) stay unchanged and are scrubbed at packaging

platform.what: a mobile (Android phone) game has Platform.json at its root, {"platform": "mobile", "orientation": "landscape" or "portrait"}, written by templates/new-game.ps1 -Platform mobile and never edited after; a game without it is a desktop game; a file that says anything else is an error, never read as desktop
platform.reader: tools/validate-game.py read_platform (python tools/validate-game.py --platform <folder> prints one JSON line: {"platform": "desktop"}, or {"platform": "mobile", "orientation", "width", "height"}); no other code parses the file
mobile: project.godot: rendering/renderer/rendering_method and rendering_method.mobile are "mobile" (never the desktop renderer forward_plus), rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc is true, display/window/size/viewport_width x viewport_height is 1920x1080 (landscape) or 1080x1920 (portrait), display/window/handheld/orientation is a landscape or a portrait setting as Platform.json says (never sensor), application/config/quit_on_go_back is false

export_presets.cfg: a preset named "Android" for the platform Android with gradle_build/use_gradle_build true, architectures/arm64-v8a true and the other three false, gradle_build/min_sdk at least 26, gradle_build/target_sdk at least 34, package/unique_name com.<project in lower case>.game
a key the file leaves out is read as Godot 4.7's default (the editor drops a setting put back to its default), never as wrong

repo.dataset_folder: Dataset/ (variant repo-dataset): checked as a dataset when manifest.json is there; a game that is not packaged yet has none (python tools/package-dataset.py <slug> writes the folder)
tasks: Tasks/<game>-<kind>-<slug>.json, one GameTask each (game-task/1: docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json), on the repo's orphan branch `tasks` (no shared history with main; a short README.md, optionally tasks-workflow.jsonl), never on main; the name field equals the file stem

the tasks branch is checked out as a git worktree outside the game folder (e.g. <root>/tasks/<slug>) and committed and pushed there; task work never enters the game's history: main tracks nothing under Tasks/ and never references the tasks branch, the recording hooks ignore commits on it, and the delivered history (History/) leaves it out
the validator and the packager read the tasks from `tasks`, else `origin/tasks`; a missing tasks branch is an error
at least 5 and up to about 10 per game (fewer than 5 is an error; more than 10 is reported, never an error or warning)
at least 4 of a game's tasks are hard (fewer is an error); the others may be medium (what a task that names no difficulty is, the schema's default), none easier

seed.game is the repo's slug; seed.commit and seed.reference are commits of main's history (ancestors of main's head) or of the task's own start branch starts/<task name>; at both, project.godot's config/features names Godot 4.7 (a start opens as committed, never upgraded)

every task is a long thread of multiple edits: never easy, tagged long-thread, with seed.reference, at least 3 required outcome probes outside still_works, and from seed.commit to seed.reference at least 5 game files (scenes/, game/, assets/, addons/ but the AutoPlay drop-in and the task probe, project.godot; a step script, an .import or a .uid is not one), 100 code lines and 2 systems, and for a seed on main 4 commits that change the game (tools/validate-game.py); everything a no-op passes weighs 0

An agent given a task starts from a history-less snapshot of the game at seed.commit with Tasks/, History/ and Dataset/ removed (they hold every task's rubrics and references): only the brief and that snapshot. The grader's half (milestones: rubrics, judge and code-judge questions, log_absent patterns; and seed.reference) never reaches the agent.

dataset.layout: docs/dataset-layout-v1.json (godot-dataset-layout/v1); tools/validate-dataset.ps1 picks the file by manifest.layout
manifest: game equals the zip's top folder (full variant)
every files[] entry exists with that size (sha256 checked by validate-dataset.ps1)
totals.files = number of files[]; totals.bytes = sum of their bytes
status complete: pending empty, replay_verification present with pass equal to report.json verdict.pass (PASS or FAIL: the verdict is metadata, the replay is required but need not pass)
replay_verification is null only while ReplayScripts/ is pending (listed in pending): the delivery is then pending, not invalid
commit equals the last commit in git.log and report.json final_commit
variant full: build is an object; repo-dataset: build is null

platform is absent or {kind desktop} for a desktop game, {kind mobile, orientation landscape or portrait} for an Android phone game, as GodotProject/Platform.json says (full variant; no file is a desktop game)

a mobile game's build may name its apk, then with package, version_code, version_name, min_sdk (at least 26) and target_sdk (at least 34), the file Build/<apk> in files[] and the package com.<project in lower case>.game; without it the delivery holds the Windows player alone (a warning); a desktop game's build names none of them
workflow: every line is one JSON object matching the row schema
a row's direction names an earlier op user.direction row
user.direction rows: actor user, reason_source user_direction, params.direction a non-empty string

the person's directions are user.direction rows, written by the session (the sessions' prompts and replies themselves are in History/sessions/messages.jsonl); a game with none is reported as a warning

banned names in rows: workflow.jsonl is append-only except that a row naming a banned term is edited in place to a neutral word or placeholder, nothing else changed, followed by one appended row op "log.correct", params {rows: [ids], what}; the commit names the edited rows (tools/scrub-workflow-rows.py). A banned name left in a row is an error, in the repo and in the dataset.
history: full variant: manifest.history is an object; History/<game>.bundle is a git bundle whose refs include history.head = manifest.commit
the bundle holds every commit (history.commits); git.log lists the same commits
every Git LFS pointer in every commit has its object under History/lfs/objects/<aa>/<bb>/<sha256>, and each object's sha256 equals its name (history.lfs_objects / lfs_bytes count them)
author and committer of every commit are dev_NN; commit messages carry no banned names (the repo's patterns; the packager's rescan also covers every text blob)

History/sessions/ (optional): messages.jsonl (every prompt the person typed and every reply the model wrote: time, session_id, role user | assistant, text) and actions.jsonl (every tool call: time, session_id, event), one JSON object per line, rows up to the release commit, each session named session_NN in both files; manifest.history.sessions counts their rows ({messages, actions}, each {file, rows}); a missing file is a note, anything wrong here a warning, never an error
brief: Brief/brief.md (the original brief) and Brief/design.md (design doc, story bible, status) are present and non-empty; manifest.brief names them
tasks: full variant: Tasks/README.md and, per task, Tasks/<name>/task.json (the agent's part) and Tasks/<name>/grader.json (milestones, seed.reference); manifest.tasks lists the names
task.json holds no milestones and no seed.reference; task.json merged with grader.json is valid against docs/schemas/game-task.schema.json
each task's name equals its folder; seed.game is the dataset's game; seed.commit and seed.reference are commits of History/<game>.bundle
at least 5 and up to about 10 per game; at least 4 of them hard; the others may be medium (what a task that names no difficulty is), none easier
repo-dataset: no Tasks/ (the repo's tasks branch is the source)

An agent given a task starts from a history-less snapshot of the game at seed.commit with Tasks/, History/ and Dataset/ removed (they hold every task's rubrics and references): only the brief and that snapshot. The grader's half (milestones: rubrics, judge and code-judge questions, log_absent patterns; and seed.reference) never reaches the agent.
